categories.name: p2p
categories.evidence: Modifies accepted socket configuration for inbound peer connections in src/net.cpp
categories.rationale: Hardens inbound P2P socket handling against potential thread stalls by explicitly setting non-blocking mode on accepted sockets. While there is no current vulnerability because POSIX calls explicitly pass MSG_DONTWAIT, author notes that relying solely on per-call flags risks allowing 'a malicious peer to stall us indefinitely for free' if a flag is ever omitted.

categories.name: rpc
categories.evidence: Modifies incoming HTTP client socket acceptance in src/httpserver.cpp
categories.rationale: Adds defensive non-blocking configuration to accepted HTTP client sockets to prevent stalling in the HTTP server. This provides belt-and-suspenders protection against socket I/O stalls on Linux, where accepted sockets do not inherit O_NONBLOCK from the listening socket.
